Cloture.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Cloture.question: A majority of three-fifths of senators duly chosen and sworn (60 votes if there is no more than one vacancy in the _____) is required for most questions
Cloture.fact: The presiding officer puts to the Senate the question, "Is it the sense of the Senate that debate shall be brought to a close?" The Senate votes on the cloture motion by the yeas and nays. A majority of three-fifths of senators duly chosen and sworn (60 votes if there is no more than one vacancy in the Senate) is required for most questions.

Cloture.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Cloture.question: Under the precedents set by the Senate on November 21, _____, and April 6, 2017, a simple majority of senators present and voting is required to invoke cloture on nominations
Cloture.fact: Under the precedents set by the Senate on November 21, 2013, and April 6, 2017, a simple majority of senators present and voting is required to invoke cloture on nominations.

Cloture.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Cloture.question: It was introduced into the _____ of the United Kingdom by William Ewart Gladstone to overcome the obstructionism of the Irish Parliamentary Party and was made permanent in 1887
Cloture.fact: Cloture (, also UK: ), closure or, informally, a guillotine, is a motion or process in parliamentary procedure aimed at bringing debate to a quick end. It was introduced into the Parliament of the United Kingdom by William Ewart Gladstone to overcome the obstructionism of the Irish Parliamentary Party and was made permanent in 1887.

Cloture.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Cloture.question: On _____ February debate began on the first resolution, on "putting the question"
Cloture.fact: The IPP MPs objected that this was an abuse by the speaker of their rights as members. The government responded by formalising the process as an amendment to the standing orders, moved by Gladstone on 3 February 1881: That, if upon Notice given a Motion be made by a Minister of the Crown that the state of Public Business is urgent, and if on the call of the Speaker 40 Members shall support it by rising in their places, the Speaker shall forthwith put the Question, no Debate, Amendment, or Adj...

Cloture.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Cloture.question: The motion on putting the question was passed, after 19 days' debate, on 10 _____ 1882: That when it shall appear to Mr
Cloture.fact: The session beginning in November 1882 was devoted entirely to the new rules. The motion on putting the question was passed, after 19 days' debate, on 10 November 1882: That when it shall appear to Mr.

Cloture.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Cloture.question: Under rule XXVIII, paragraph 2, added in January _____, a cloture motion on a compound motion to go to conference ripens two hours after it is filed
Cloture.fact: Under rule XXII, paragraph 3, added in January 2013, a cloture motion signed by 16 senators (including the majority leader, minority leader, 7 other majority senators and 7 other minority senators) presented on a motion to proceed ripens one hour after the Senate convenes on the following calendar day. Under rule XXVIII, paragraph 2, added in January 2013, a cloture motion on a compound motion to go to conference ripens two hours after it is filed.

CMYK color model.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
CMYK color model.question: The _____ was Subtractive color model used in printing.
CMYK color model.fact: The CMYK color model is a subtractive color model used in color printing as well as describing the printing process.

CMYK color model.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
CMYK color model.question: Extended gamut systems (e.g., CMYKOG _____) increase the range of reproducible colors beyond standard CMYK
CMYK color model.fact: Extended gamut systems (e.g., CMYKOG Hexachrome) increase the range of reproducible colors beyond standard CMYK.

CMYK color model.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
CMYK color model.question: Conversion depends on device gamuts, rendering intents, and factors such as dot gain and _____ primaries
CMYK color model.fact: Conversion depends on device gamuts, rendering intents, and factors such as dot gain and Neugebauer primaries.

CMYK color model.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
CMYK color model.question: Predefined printing standards, such as Specifications for _____, include ICC profiles for software and operating systems
CMYK color model.fact: Predefined printing standards, such as Specifications for Web Offset Publications, include ICC profiles for software and operating systems.

Coated paper.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Coated paper.question: The _____ was Paper coated with a compound or polymer.
Coated paper.fact: Coated paper (also called enamel paper, gloss paper, and thin paper) is paper that has been coated with a mixture of materials or a polymer to impart certain qualities to the paper, including weight, surface gloss, smoothness, or reduced ink absorbency.

Coated paper.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Coated paper.question: Biopolymer coatings are available as more sustainable alternatives to common petrochemical coatings like low-density polyethylene (_____) or mylar
Coated paper.fact: Biopolymer coatings are available as more sustainable alternatives to common petrochemical coatings like low-density polyethylene (LDPE) or mylar.

Coated paper.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Coated paper.question: Plastic is used to enhance properties such as water resistance, tear strength, abrasion resistance, and _____, etc
Coated paper.fact: Plastic is used to enhance properties such as water resistance, tear strength, abrasion resistance, and heat sealability, etc.

Coated paper.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Coated paper.question: Most plastic coatings in the packaging industry are polyethylene (_____) and to a much lesser degree PET
Coated paper.fact: Most plastic coatings in the packaging industry are polyethylene (LDPE) and to a much lesser degree PET.

Coated paper.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Coated paper.question: (see _____ paper) Paper labels are often coated with adhesive (pressure sensitive or gummed) on one side and coated with printing or graphics on the other
Coated paper.fact: (see Thermal paper) Paper labels are often coated with adhesive (pressure sensitive or gummed) on one side and coated with printing or graphics on the other.

Cognitive grammar.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Cognitive grammar.question: The _____ was Linguistic theory.
Cognitive grammar.fact: Cognitive grammar is a cognitive approach to language developed by Ronald Langacker, which hypothesizes that grammar, semantics, and lexicon exist on a continuum instead of as separate processes altogether.

Cognitive grammar.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Cognitive grammar.question: Volume one is titled "_____", and it explores Langacker's hypothesis that grammar may be deconstructed into patterns that come together in order to represent concepts
Cognitive grammar.fact: Volume one is titled "Theoretical Prerequisites", and it explores Langacker's hypothesis that grammar may be deconstructed into patterns that come together in order to represent concepts.

Cognitive grammar.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Cognitive grammar.question: Volume two is titled "_____", as it moves beyond the first volume to elaborate on the ways in which Langacker's previously described theories may be applied
Cognitive grammar.fact: Volume two is titled "Descriptive Application", as it moves beyond the first volume to elaborate on the ways in which Langacker's previously described theories may be applied.

Cognitive grammar.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Cognitive grammar.question: Langacker invites his reader to utilize the tools presented in the first volume of _____ in a wide range of, mainly English, grammatical situations
Cognitive grammar.fact: Langacker invites his reader to utilize the tools presented in the first volume of Foundations in a wide range of, mainly English, grammatical situations.

Cognitive grammar.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Cognitive grammar.question: It primarily diverges from _____ tradition through its assertion that grammar and language are integral and essential parts of cognition, not merely autonomous processes in the brain
Cognitive grammar.fact: It primarily diverges from Chomskyan tradition through its assertion that grammar and language are integral and essential parts of cognition, not merely autonomous processes in the brain.

Cognitive synonymy.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Cognitive synonymy.question: The _____ was Synonyms indistinguishable in meaning.
Cognitive synonymy.fact: Cognitive synonymy is a type of synonymy in which synonyms are so similar in meaning that they cannot be differentiated either denotatively or connotatively, that is, not even by mental associations, connotations, emotive responses, and poetic value.

Cognitive synonymy.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Cognitive synonymy.question: Willard Van Orman Quine used the concept of cognitive synonymy extensively in his famous _____ paper "Two Dogmas of Empiricism", where two words were cognitively synonymous if they were interchangeabl
Cognitive synonymy.fact: Willard Van Orman Quine used the concept of cognitive synonymy extensively in his famous 1951 paper "Two Dogmas of Empiricism", where two words were cognitively synonymous if they were interchangeable in every possible instance.

Cognitive synonymy.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Cognitive synonymy.question: Quine notes that if one is referring to the word itself, this doesn't apply, as in, _____ has fewer than ten letters
Cognitive synonymy.fact: For example, All bachelors are unmarried men. Quine notes that if one is referring to the word itself, this doesn't apply, as in, Bachelor has fewer than ten letters.

Cognitive synonymy.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Cognitive synonymy.question: As compared to the substitution which is obviously false, "_____ men" has less than ten letters
Cognitive synonymy.fact: For example, All bachelors are unmarried men. All unmarried men are not married.

Collective.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Collective.question: The _____ was Group of entities sharing interest.
Collective.fact: A collective is a group of entities that share or are motivated by at least one common issue or interest or work together to achieve a common objective. Collectives can differ from cooperatives in that they are not necessarily focused upon an economic benefit or saving, though they can be.

College tour.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
College tour.question: The _____ was College event for prospective students.
College tour.fact: A college tour, also called a campus tour, is a tour of a college or university's campus. College tours may be taken individually or by school groups and educational programs as a way for many people to visit several schools over a short period of time.

College tour.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
College tour.question: In addition, many colleges now offer virtual tours on the _____
College tour.fact: In addition, many colleges now offer virtual tours on the Internet.

Color printing.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Color printing.question: The _____ was Reproductive printing with color.
Color printing.fact: Color printing or colour printing is the reproduction of an image or text in color (as opposed to simpler black and white or monochrome printing).

Color printing.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Color printing.question: The earliest way of adding color to items printed on paper was by hand-coloring, and this was widely used for printed images in both Europe and _____
Color printing.fact: The earliest way of adding color to items printed on paper was by hand-coloring, and this was widely used for printed images in both Europe and East Asia.

Color printing.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Color printing.question: However this became much rarer after about _____
Color printing.fact: However this became much rarer after about 1500.

Color printing.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Color printing.question: Color prints were also used later in the _____
Color printing.fact: Color prints were also used later in the Ming Dynasty.

Color printing.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Color printing.question: The first known example is a book on ink-cakes printed in _____, and color technique reached its height in books on painting published in the seventeenth century
Color printing.fact: The first known example is a book on ink-cakes printed in 1606, and color technique reached its height in books on painting published in the seventeenth century.

Color printing.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Color printing.question: Notable examples are Ming-era Chinese painter Hu Zhengyan's Treatise on the Paintings and Writings of the Ten Bamboo Studio of _____, and the Manual of the Mustard Seed Garden published in 1679 and 17
Color printing.fact: Notable examples are Ming-era Chinese painter Hu Zhengyan's Treatise on the Paintings and Writings of the Ten Bamboo Studio of 1633, and the Manual of the Mustard Seed Garden published in 1679 and 1701, and printed in five colors.

Color printing.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Color printing.question: For instance: _____-e (藍摺り絵, "indigo printed pictures"), Murasaki-e (紫絵, "purple pictures"), and other styles in which a single color would be used in addition to, or instead of, black ink
Color printing.fact: For instance: Aizuri-e (藍摺り絵, "indigo printed pictures"), Murasaki-e (紫絵, "purple pictures"), and other styles in which a single color would be used in addition to, or instead of, black ink.

Color printing.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Color printing.question: This was the method developed in _____; in Italy only tone blocks were often used, to create an effect more like a wash drawing
Color printing.fact: This was the method developed in Germany; in Italy only tone blocks were often used, to create an effect more like a wash drawing.

Color printing.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Color printing.question: George Baxter patented in _____ a method using an intaglio line plate (or occasionally a lithograph), printed in black or a dark color, and then overprinted with up to twenty different colors from woo
Color printing.fact: George Baxter patented in 1835 a method using an intaglio line plate (or occasionally a lithograph), printed in black or a dark color, and then overprinted with up to twenty different colors from woodblocks.

Color printing.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Color printing.question: English Artists such as _____, Walter Crane and Kate Greenaway were influenced by the Japanese prints now available and fashionable in Europe to create a suitable style, with flat areas of color
Color printing.fact: English Artists such as Randolph Caldecott, Walter Crane and Kate Greenaway were influenced by the Japanese prints now available and fashionable in Europe to create a suitable style, with flat areas of color.

Column (typography).subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Column (typography).question: The _____ was Vertical block of content on a page.
Column (typography).fact: In typography, a column is one or more vertical blocks of content positioned on a page, separated by gutters or alleys (vertical whitespace) or rules (thin lines, in this case vertical). Columns are most commonly used to break up large bodies of text that cannot fit in a single block of text on a page.

Column (typography).subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Column (typography).question: One method of creating columns for the web is to place text within an _____ table element, often with the border set to zero
Column (typography).fact: One method of creating columns for the web is to place text within an HTML table element, often with the border set to zero. These methods were not as straightforward as using HTML tables, which made a tableless three column layout a sort of holy grail once these techniques were discovered in the early 2000s.

Column (typography).subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Column (typography).question: These methods were not as straightforward as using _____ tables, which made a tableless three column layout a sort of holy grail once these techniques were discovered in the early 2000s

These methods were not as straightforward as using HTML tables, which made a tableless three column layout a sort of holy grail once these techniques were discovered in the early 2000s.

Community.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Community.question: The _____ was Social unit which shares commonality.
Community.fact: A community is a social unit (a group of people) with one or more shared socially-significant characteristics, being place, set of norms, culture, religion, values, customs, or identity. Durable good relations that extend beyond immediate genealogical ties also define a sense of community, important to people's identity, practice, and roles in social institutions such as family, home, work, government, society, or humanity at large.

Community.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Community.question: Species interact in three ways: competition, predation and mutualism: _____ typically results in a double negative—that is both species lose in the interaction
Community.fact: Species interact in three ways: competition, predation and mutualism: Competition typically results in a double negative—that is both species lose in the interaction.

Community.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Community.question: Such early academic studies include _____? by Robert Dahl as well as the papers by Floyd Hunter on Atlanta
Community.fact: Such early academic studies include Who Governs? by Robert Dahl as well as the papers by Floyd Hunter on Atlanta.

Community.question: Tönnies proposed the _____–Gesellschaft dichotomy as a way to think about social ties
Community.fact: Tönnies proposed the Gemeinschaft–Gesellschaft dichotomy as a way to think about social ties. Gemeinschaft stress personal social interactions, and the roles, values, and beliefs based on such interactions.

Community.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Community.question: Emptiness: _____ beyond the attempts to fix, heal and convert of the chaos stage, when all people become capable of acknowledging their own woundedness and brokenness, common to human beings
Community.fact: Emptiness: Moves beyond the attempts to fix, heal and convert of the chaos stage, when all people become capable of acknowledging their own woundedness and brokenness, common to human beings.

Community.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Community.question: In _____, Peck remarked that building a sense of community is easy but maintaining this sense of community is difficult in the modern world
Community.fact: In 1991, Peck remarked that building a sense of community is easy but maintaining this sense of community is difficult in the modern world.

Community.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Community.question: An interview with M. _____ by Alan Atkisson
Community.fact: An interview with M. Scott Peck by Alan Atkisson.

Community.question: Rebekah Nathan suggests in her book, _____, we are drawn to developing communities totally based on sameness, despite stated commitments to diversity, such as those found on university websites
Community.fact: Rebekah Nathan suggests in her book, My Freshman Year, we are drawn to developing communities totally based on sameness, despite stated commitments to diversity, such as those found on university websites.

Community.question: One such breakdown is as follows: _____-based: range from the local neighbourhood, suburb, village, town or city, region, nation or even the planet as a whole
Community.fact: If communities are developed based on something they share in common, whether location or values, then one challenge for developing communities is how to incorporate individuality and differences. One such breakdown is as follows: Location-based: range from the local neighbourhood, suburb, village, town or city, region, nation or even the planet as a whole.

Community.fact: A survey conducted by Pew Internet and The American Life Project in 2001 found those involved in entertainment, professional, and sports virtual-groups focused their activities on obtaining information.

Community.fact: A survey conducted by Pew Internet and The American Life Project in 2001 found those involved in entertainment, professional, and sports virtual-groups focused their activities on obtaining information.

Complex text layout.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Complex text layout.question: The _____ was Neighbour-dependent grapheme positioning.
Complex text layout.fact: Complex text layout (CTL) or complex text rendering is the typesetting of writing systems in which the shape or positioning of a grapheme depends on its relation to other graphemes.

Complex text layout.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Complex text layout.question: Examples include the _____ script and scripts of the Brahmic family, such as Devanagari, Khmer script or the Thai script
Complex text layout.fact: Examples include the Arabic script and scripts of the Brahmic family, such as Devanagari, Khmer script or the Thai script.

Complex text layout.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Complex text layout.question: For instance, the Latin script or _____ characters can be typeset by simply displaying each character one after another in straight rows or columns
Complex text layout.fact: For instance, the Latin script or Chinese characters can be typeset by simply displaying each character one after another in straight rows or columns.

Complex text layout.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Complex text layout.question: For example, a character in _____ script can have as many as four different shape-forms, depending on context
Complex text layout.fact: For example, a character in Arabic script can have as many as four different shape-forms, depending on context.

Complex text layout.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Complex text layout.question: For example, the _____ alphabet has context-sensitive shaping of the letter sigma, which appears as ς at the end of a word and σ elsewhere
Complex text layout.fact: For example, the Greek alphabet has context-sensitive shaping of the letter sigma, which appears as ς at the end of a word and σ elsewhere. However, these two forms are normally stored as different characters; for instance, Unicode has both U+03C2 ς GREEK SMALL LETTER FINAL SIGMA and U+03C3 σ GREEK SMALL LETTER SIGMA, and does not treat them as equivalent.

Complex text layout.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Complex text layout.question: Examples of this latter approach include _____ (AAT) and Graphite
Complex text layout.fact: Examples of this latter approach include Apple Advanced Typography (AAT) and Graphite.

Complex text layout.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Complex text layout.question: Both of these names encompass both the instruction format and the software supporting it; AAT is included on Apple operating systems, while Graphite is available for _____ and Linux-based systems
Complex text layout.fact: Both of these names encompass both the instruction format and the software supporting it; AAT is included on Apple operating systems, while Graphite is available for Microsoft Windows and Linux-based systems.

Complex text layout.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Complex text layout.question: AAT and _____ instructions can be embedded in OpenType font files
Complex text layout.fact: Examples of this latter approach include Apple Advanced Typography (AAT) and Graphite. Both of these names encompass both the instruction format and the software supporting it; AAT is included on Apple operating systems, while Graphite is available for Microsoft Windows and Linux-based systems.

Computational linguistics.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Computational linguistics.question: The _____ was Use of computational tools for the study of linguistics.
Computational linguistics.fact: Computational linguistics is an interdisciplinary field concerned with the computational modelling of natural language, as well as the study of appropriate computational approaches to linguistic questions. In general, computational linguistics draws upon linguistics, computer science, artificial intelligence, mathematics, logic, philosophy, cognitive science, cognitive psychology, psycholinguistics, anthropology and neuroscience, among others.

Computational linguistics.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Computational linguistics.question: Attempts have been made to determine how an infant learns a "non-normal grammar" as theorized by _____ normal form
Computational linguistics.fact: Attempts have been made to determine how an infant learns a "non-normal grammar" as theorized by Chomsky normal form.

Computational linguistics.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Computational linguistics.question: Research in this area combines structural approaches with computational models to analyze large linguistic corpora like the _____, helping to uncover patterns in language acquisition
Computational linguistics.fact: Research in this area combines structural approaches with computational models to analyze large linguistic corpora like the Penn Treebank, helping to uncover patterns in language acquisition.

Computational linguistics.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Computational linguistics.question: It consisted of IBM computer manuals, transcribed telephone conversations, and other texts, together containing over _____ words of American English, annotated using both part-of-speech tagging and sy
Computational linguistics.fact: It consisted of IBM computer manuals, transcribed telephone conversations, and other texts, together containing over 4.5 million words of American English, annotated using both part-of-speech tagging and syntactic bracketing.

Computer font.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Computer font.question: The _____ was Digital description of a typographical font.
Computer font.fact: A computer font or digital font is a digital data file containing a set of graphically related glyphs, usually designed and created using a font editor.

Computer font.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Computer font.question: (for example, _____ bold 12 point)
Computer font.fact: In the terminology of movable metal type, a typeface is a set of characters that share common design features across styles and sizes (for example, all the varieties of Gill Sans), while a font is a set of pieces of movable type in a specific typeface, size, width, weight, slope, etc. (for example, Gill Sans bold 12 point).

Computer font.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Computer font.question: In _____, CSS, and related technologies, the font family attribute refers to the digital equivalent of a typeface
Computer font.fact: In HTML, CSS, and related technologies, the font family attribute refers to the digital equivalent of a typeface.

Computer font.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Computer font.question: Advantages of bitmap fonts include: _____ fast and simple to render Easier to create than other kinds
Computer font.fact: Advantages of bitmap fonts include: Extremely fast and simple to render Easier to create than other kinds.

Computer font.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Computer font.question: Bitmap fonts are used in the Linux console, the _____ recovery console, and embedded systems
Computer font.fact: Bitmap fonts are used in the Linux console, the Windows recovery console, and embedded systems.

Computer font.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Computer font.fact: For example, the original Apple Macintosh computer could produce bold by widening vertical strokes and oblique by shearing the image.

Computer font.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Computer font.question: Bitmap fonts are like image formats such as Windows Bitmap (.bmp), _____ (.png) and Tagged Image Format (.tif or .tiff), which store the image data as a grid of pixels, in some cases with compression
Computer font.fact: Bitmap fonts are like image formats such as Windows Bitmap (.bmp), Portable Network Graphics (.png) and Tagged Image Format (.tif or .tiff), which store the image data as a grid of pixels, in some cases with compression.

Computer font.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Computer font.question: The advent of desktop publishing brought the need for a common standard to integrate the graphical user interface of the first _____ and laser printers
Computer font.fact: The advent of desktop publishing brought the need for a common standard to integrate the graphical user interface of the first Macintosh and laser printers.

Computer font.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Computer font.question: The term to describe the integration technology was WYSIWYG (_____ Get)
Computer font.answer: What You See Is What You
Computer font.fact: The term to describe the integration technology was WYSIWYG (What You See Is What You Get).

Computer font.question: Examples of outline fonts include Post_____ 1 and Type 3 fonts, TrueType, OpenType and Compugraphic
Computer font.fact: Examples of outline fonts include PostScript Type 1 and Type 3 fonts, TrueType, OpenType and Compugraphic.

Computer font.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Computer font.question: Unlike Type 1 fonts, _____Type glyphs are described with quadratic Bézier curves
Computer font.fact: Unlike Type 1 fonts, TrueType glyphs are described with quadratic Bézier curves. OpenType fonts contain outlines in either the TrueType or CFF format together with a wide range of metadata.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: The oldest parts in the surviving version of the text probably date to about _____ BCE
Draupadi.fact: The oldest parts in the surviving version of the text probably date to about 400 BCE.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Pandavas, along with Kunti and _____, proceed to the royal residence, where Drupada has arranged displays representing various trades and social classes
Draupadi.fact: Pandavas, along with Kunti and Drupadi, proceed to the royal residence, where Drupada has arranged displays representing various trades and social classes. Kunti and Drupadi withdraw to the women's quarters while Drupada announces that Drupadi will marry Arjuna upon confirming Pandavas' identities.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Kunti and _____ withdraw to the women's quarters while Drupada announces that Drupadi will marry Arjuna upon confirming Pandavas' identities
Draupadi.fact: Pandavas, along with Kunti and Drupadi, proceed to the royal residence, where Drupada has arranged displays representing various trades and social classes. Kunti and Drupadi withdraw to the women's quarters while Drupada announces that Drupadi will marry Arjuna upon confirming Pandavas' identities.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: At that moment, the divine-sage _____ arrives and is asked to give his opinion
Draupadi.fact: At that moment, the divine-sage Vyasa arrives and is asked to give his opinion. Vyasa ultimately approves the arrangement and retires with Drupada to the inner chambers for further discussion, where the second and third justificatons behind Draupadi is disclosed.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: He listens to each viewpoint: _____ opposes the marriage, Dhrishtadyumna remains undecided, while Yudhishthira and Kunti support it
Draupadi.fact: Drupada furiously protests, questioning the propriety of such a union. He listens to each viewpoint: Drupada opposes the marriage, Dhrishtadyumna remains undecided, while Yudhishthira and Kunti support it.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Vyasa narrates that once, during a twelve-year-long yajna conducted by _____, the god of death, on the banks of the Ganga, no death occurs in the world
Draupadi.fact: Vyasa narrates that once, during a twelve-year-long yajna conducted by Yama, the god of death, on the banks of the Ganga, no death occurs in the world.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Amid this cosmic pause, _____ appears in enigmatic form—a weeping, alluring figure whose tears transform into golden lotuses as they fall into the river
Draupadi.fact: Amid this cosmic pause, Shri appears in enigmatic form—a weeping, alluring figure whose tears transform into golden lotuses as they fall into the river.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Her presence captivates _____, who follows the trail of these lotuses to encounter the god Shiva, engaged in a game of dice with his consort
Draupadi.fact: Her presence captivates Indra, who follows the trail of these lotuses to encounter the god Shiva, engaged in a game of dice with his consort. However, Indra fails to recognise Shiva and speaks to him disrespectfully.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: However, _____ fails to recognise Shiva and speaks to him disrespectfully
Draupadi.fact: Her presence captivates Indra, who follows the trail of these lotuses to encounter the god Shiva, engaged in a game of dice with his consort. However, Indra fails to recognise Shiva and speaks to him disrespectfully.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: As a consequence, Shiva curses him and sends him to a cave-like netherworld, where four other proud Indras—_____, Bhūtadhāma, Śibi, Śānti, and Tejasvī—are already imprisoned
Draupadi.fact: As a consequence, Shiva curses him and sends him to a cave-like netherworld, where four other proud Indras—Vishvabhuk, Bhūtadhāma, Śibi, Śānti, and Tejasvī—are already imprisoned.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: These five celestial beings are later reborn on earth as the five _____ brothers
Draupadi.fact: These five celestial beings are later reborn on earth as the five Pandava brothers. This association of Draupadi with Shri directly connects her to kingship: the Pandavas' legitimacy to rule is symbolically reinforced through their union with Shri incarnate.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: In this account, the sage's daughter performs severe austerities and pleases the god _____, to whom she prays with the desire for a virtuous husband
Draupadi.fact: In this account, the sage's daughter performs severe austerities and pleases the god Shiva, to whom she prays with the desire for a virtuous husband. Shiva, in response, grants her the boon that she will have five virtuous husbands in her next life.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: This account, absent in the _____ version of the epic, is widely regarded by scholars as a later interpolation and is excluded from the Critical Edition
Draupadi.fact: This account, absent in the Northern version of the epic, is widely regarded by scholars as a later interpolation and is excluded from the Critical Edition.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: According to this version, _____ is the devoted wife of the sage Maudgalya, a man afflicted with leprosy, old age, and a foul temper
Draupadi.fact: According to this version, Nalayani is the devoted wife of the sage Maudgalya, a man afflicted with leprosy, old age, and a foul temper.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Pleased by her loyalty, _____ offers her a boon
Draupadi.fact: According to this version, Nalayani is the devoted wife of the sage Maudgalya, a man afflicted with leprosy, old age, and a foul temper. Pleased by her loyalty, Maudgalya offers her a boon.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: After thousands of years of this life, _____ grows tired and returns to asceticism
Draupadi.fact: Pleased by her loyalty, Maudgalya offers her a boon. Maudgalya agrees, and the two roam the world for many years in different forms.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Grieved by the curse, _____ performs severe penance
Draupadi.fact: Nalayani begs him to continue their pleasures, but he becomes angry and curses her to be reborn as a woman who will have five husbands to satisfy her. Grieved by the curse, Nalayani performs severe penance.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: With the _____' survival revealed, Dhritrashtra invites the Pandavas to Hastinapura and proposes that the kingdom be divided
Draupadi.fact: Kunti blesses Draupadi to lead the Pandavas, while Krishna sends gifts for her. With the Pandavas' survival revealed, Dhritrashtra invites the Pandavas to Hastinapura and proposes that the kingdom be divided.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: The Pandavas are assigned the unreclaimed desert _____, which they rebuild into the glorious Indraprastha with divine help
Draupadi.fact: The Pandavas are assigned the unreclaimed desert Khandavaprastha, which they rebuild into the glorious Indraprastha with divine help.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Despite the practice of polyandry, the sons are recognized as legitimate and are collectively known as the _____
Draupadi.fact: Despite the practice of polyandry, the sons are recognized as legitimate and are collectively called the Draupadeyas. Ashwatthama later kills the Draupadeyas during his surprise raid on Pandava camp on the eighteenth day of the war to avenge the death of his father Drona.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Ashwatthama later kills the _____ during his surprise raid on Pandava camp on the eighteenth day of the war to avenge the death of his father Drona
Draupadi.fact: Despite the practice of polyandry, the sons are recognized as legitimate and are collectively called the Draupadeyas. Ashwatthama later kills the Draupadeyas during his surprise raid on Pandava camp on the eighteenth day of the war to avenge the death of his father Drona.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Their names are _____ (fathered by Yudhishthira), Sutasoma (fathered by Bhima), Shrutakarma (fathered by Arjuna), Satanika (fathered by Nakula) and Shrutasena (fathered by Sahadeva)
Draupadi.fact: Their names are Prativindhya (fathered by Yudhishthira), Sutasoma (fathered by Bhima), Shrutakarma (fathered by Arjuna), Satanika (fathered by Nakula) and Shrutasena (fathered by Sahadeva).

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: In the _____, four defining characteristics are attributed to her status: she is priyā (beloved), darśanīyā (beautiful), paṇḍitā (learned), and pativratā (dedicated to her husband)
Draupadi.fact: In the Mahabharata, four defining characteristics are attributed to her status: she is priyā (beloved), darśanīyā (beautiful), paṇḍitā (learned), and pativratā (dedicated to her husband).

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: At the end of this exile, _____ returns with his new bride—Subhadra, the sister of Krishna
Draupadi.fact: A notable incident during this period occurs when Arjuna breaks the pact made among the brothers by entering Draupadi's chamber while she is with Yudhishthira, in order to retrieve his weapons. At the end of this exile, Arjuna returns with his new bride—Subhadra, the sister of Krishna.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: While exploring the palace during the _____ yajna, Duryodhana mistakes a polished floor for solid ground and falls into a hidden pool
Draupadi.fact: Following this, Yudhishthira performs the Rajasuya yajna with Draupadi by his side; the Pandavas gains lordship over many regions. Draupadi's role during the Rajasuya is revealed by Duryodhana, who reports to his father that how he had observed Draupadi serving food to everyone, including physically challenged citizens.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: However, this account is absent from the original _____ and appears to originate from a much later dramatic retelling
Draupadi.fact: However, this account is absent from the original Mahabharata and appears to originate from a much later dramatic retelling.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: In the original _____ epic, the incident unfolds differently
Draupadi.fact: In the original Sanskrit epic, the incident unfolds differently.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Bhima, Arjuna, Nakula, and _____, along with their entourages, witness Duryodhana's fall and laugh at his misfortune
Draupadi.fact: Born from a yajna (fire sacrifice) conducted by King Drupada of Panchala, she is the princess of the Panchala Kingdom and the common wife of the five Pandava brothers—Yudhishthira, Bhima, Arjuna, Nakula, and Sahadeva—in a polyandrous marriage sanctioned by divine prophecy and narratives of her previous lives.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Despite this, _____ feels deeply humiliated by the reaction of the Pandavas and their servants
Draupadi.fact: Bhima, Arjuna, Nakula, and Sahadeva, along with their entourages, witness Duryodhana's fall and laugh at his misfortune. Despite this, Duryodhana feels deeply humiliated by the reaction of the Pandavas and their servants.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Upon returning to _____, he voices his anguish to his father, expressing resentment over the Pandavas' prosperity, which had been bolstered by the Rajasuya yajna
Draupadi.fact: Upon returning to Hastinapura, he voices his anguish to his father, expressing resentment over the Pandavas' prosperity, which had been bolstered by the Rajasuya yajna.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: It is one of the driving reasons that ultimately led to the _____
Draupadi.fact: It is one of the driving reasons that ultimately led to the Kurukshetra War.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Together with his maternal uncle _____, Duryodhana conspired to call on the Pandavas to Hastinapura and win their kingdoms in a game of gambling
Draupadi.fact: Together with his maternal uncle Shakuni, Duryodhana conspired to call on the Pandavas to Hastinapura and win their kingdoms in a game of gambling. There is famous folklore that the plan's architect, Shakuni had magic dice that would never disobey his will, as they were made from the bones of Shakuni's father.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: There is famous folklore that the plan's architect, _____ had magic dice that would never disobey his will, as they were made from the bones of Shakuni's father
Draupadi.fact: Together with his maternal uncle Shakuni, Duryodhana conspired to call on the Pandavas to Hastinapura and win their kingdoms in a game of gambling. There is famous folklore that the plan's architect, Shakuni had magic dice that would never disobey his will, as they were made from the bones of Shakuni's father.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: This story, however, is non-existent in the _____ epic
Draupadi.fact: This story, however, is non-existent in the Sanskrit epic.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: As the game proceeds, _____ loses everything at first
Draupadi.fact: As the game proceeds, Yudhishthira loses everything at first. In the second round, Yudhishthira's brother Nakula is at stake, and Yudhishthira loses him.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: In the second round, _____'s brother Nakula is at stake, and Yudhishthira loses him
Draupadi.fact: As the game proceeds, Yudhishthira loses everything at first. In the second round, Yudhishthira's brother Nakula is at stake, and Yudhishthira loses him.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Finally, _____ puts himself at stake, and loses again
Draupadi.fact: As the game proceeds, Yudhishthira loses everything at first. In the second round, Yudhishthira's brother Nakula is at stake, and Yudhishthira loses him.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Yudhisthira subsequently gambles away _____, Arjuna and Bhima
Draupadi.fact: Yudhisthira subsequently gambles away Sahadeva, Arjuna and Bhima.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: For Duryodhana, the humiliation of the _____ was not complete
Draupadi.fact: For Duryodhana, the humiliation of the Pandavas was not complete.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Playing the next round, _____ wins
Draupadi.fact: Playing the next round, Shakuni wins.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: The enraged Bhima vows in front of the entire assembly that he would break _____'s thighs, or else accept being Duryodhana's slave for seven lifetimes
Draupadi.fact: In order to provoke the Pandavas further, Duryodhana bares and pats his thigh looking into Draupadi's eyes, implying that she should sit on his thigh. The enraged Bhima vows in front of the entire assembly that he would break Duryodhana's thighs, or else accept being Duryodhana's slave for seven lifetimes.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: At this point, a furious Bhima vows to drink blood from _____'s chest, at the pain of not seeing his ancestors entering heaven
Draupadi.fact: Dushasana attempts to disrobe her, but she is miraculously protected when Dushasana finds that as he continues to unwrap the layers of her sari, the amount of fabric covering her never lessens. Dushasana is eventually reduced to exhaustion, as the awed court observes that Draupadi is still chastely dressed.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Vidura openly calls _____ a snake and demon after finding no support even from his own brother, Vidura is helpless
Draupadi.fact: Vidura openly calls Duryodhana a snake and demon after finding no support even from his own brother, Vidura is helpless.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Queen Gandhari enters the scene and counsels _____ to undo her sons' misdeeds
Draupadi.fact: Queen Gandhari enters the scene and counsels Dhritarashtra to undo her sons' misdeeds. Fearing the ill-omens, Dhritarashtra intervenes and grants Draupadi a boon.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: In order to pacify her further, _____ offers a second boon
Draupadi.fact: Queen Gandhari enters the scene and counsels Dhritarashtra to undo her sons' misdeeds. Fearing the ill-omens, Dhritarashtra intervenes and grants Draupadi a boon.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Calmly, she asks for the freedom of the _____ along with their weapons
Draupadi.fact: Calmly, she asks for the freedom of the Pandavas along with their weapons. Amused by the sudden turn of events, Karna remarks that they "have never heard of such an act, performed by any of the women noted in this world for their beauty." He taunts the Pandavas by praising their wife, as she had rescued them "like a boat from their ocean of distress".

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Narrative accounts within this _____ describe several key episodes
Draupadi.fact: Narrative accounts within this Parva describe several key episodes.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: A widely popular narrative, though considered by scholars to be an interpolation, recounts an incident during this period involving sage _____
Draupadi.fact: A widely popular narrative, though considered by scholars to be an interpolation, recounts an incident during this period involving sage Durvasa. According to this account, after Draupadi and the Pandavas had finished their meal prepared using the Akshay Patra, Durvasa and his disciples arrived unexpectedly.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Sent by _____ with the intent of having the sage curse the Pandavas, they were received with hospitality
Draupadi.fact: Sent by Duryodhana with the intent of having the sage curse the Pandavas, they were received with hospitality.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Fearing the sage's potential curse, she prayed to _____
Draupadi.fact: Fearing the sage's potential curse, she prayed to Krishna. In response, Krishna requested the vessel from Draupadi, and upon consuming a single grain of rice remaining within, both Durvasa and his disciples experienced a sensation of having eaten a lavish meal.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Notably, this incident is absent from the _____ of the Mahabharata
Draupadi.fact: Notably, this incident is absent from the Critical Edition of the Mahabharata.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: At this time _____, the son of Vriddhakshatra and the husband of Duryodhana's sister Dussala, passed through Kamyaka forest on the way to Salva Desa
Draupadi.fact: At this time Jayadratha, the son of Vriddhakshatra and the husband of Duryodhana's sister Dussala, passed through Kamyaka forest on the way to Salva Desa. Jayadratha met Draupadi and then started beseeching her to go away with him and desert her husband.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Failing with words, _____ forced her onto his chariot
Draupadi.fact: At this time Jayadratha, the son of Vriddhakshatra and the husband of Duryodhana's sister Dussala, passed through Kamyaka forest on the way to Salva Desa. Jayadratha met Draupadi and then started beseeching her to go away with him and desert her husband.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Learning of their wife's abduction by _____ they rushed to save her
Draupadi.fact: Draupadi pointed out the immorality of deserting one's spouses when they were in difficulty and attempted to stall and dissuade Jayadratha by describing how the Pandavas would punish him. Failing with words, Jayadratha forced her onto his chariot.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Before freeing him, the _____ shaved Jayadratha's head at five places in order to publicly humiliate him
Draupadi.fact: On seeing the Pandavas coming after him, Jayadratha left Draupadi on the road, though ultimately the Pandavas managed to arrest him. Before freeing him, the Pandavas shaved Jayadratha's head at five places in order to publicly humiliate him.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Seeing his persistence, she warns _____ that her husbands are very strong and that he will not be able to escape death at their hands
Draupadi.fact: One day Kichaka, Sudeshna's brother and the commander of king Virata's forces, happens to see Draupadi. Seeing his persistence, she warns Kichaka that her husbands are very strong and that he will not be able to escape death at their hands.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Kichaka kicks her in front of all the courtiers, including _____
Draupadi.fact: Kichaka kicks her in front of all the courtiers, including Yudhishthira. Bhima is present, and only a look from Yudhishthira prevents him from attacking Kichaka.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Bhima is present, and only a look from _____ prevents him from attacking Kichaka
Draupadi.fact: Kichaka kicks her in front of all the courtiers, including Yudhishthira. Bhima is present, and only a look from Yudhishthira prevents him from attacking Kichaka.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Fearful of losing his most powerful warrior, even _____ does not take any action
Draupadi.fact: Draupadi escapes and runs into the court of Virata. Fearful of losing his most powerful warrior, even Virat does not take any action.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: She then curses _____ with death by her husband's hand
Draupadi.fact: Bhima is present, and only a look from Yudhishthira prevents him from attacking Kichaka. She then curses Kichaka with death by her husband's hand.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Laughing it off, _____ only doubts their whereabouts and asks those present where the Gandharvas are
Draupadi.fact: Bhima is present, and only a look from Yudhishthira prevents him from attacking Kichaka. She then curses Kichaka with death by her husband's hand.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: With this, the king asks _____ to leave and praises Yudhishthira's reply as he himself could not think of anything
Draupadi.fact: She then curses Kichaka with death by her husband's hand. Laughing it off, Kichaka only doubts their whereabouts and asks those present where the Gandharvas are.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: The murder is attributed to her _____ husbands
Draupadi.fact: The murder is attributed to her Gandharva husbands.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: This angers _____'s brothers and they decide to burn her along with Kichaka's body to take revenge
Draupadi.fact: Bhima (in the guise of Draupadi), fights with Kichaka and kills him. Draupadi calls the members of Kichaka's family and shows them the mutilated body of Kichaka.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Upon her pleading, Bhima runs for her help and kills the brothers of _____, thus saving her from being burnt alive
Draupadi.fact: This angers Kichaka's brothers and they decide to burn her along with Kichaka's body to take revenge. After getting permission from Virata, Draupadi is forcefully tied to Kichaka's pyre.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: However, the _____ refused, escalating tensions and leading to the Kurukshetra War
Draupadi.fact: However, the Kauravas refused, escalating tensions and leading to the Kurukshetra War.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Krishna, acting as a peace emissary, attempted to negotiate with _____, seeking to secure the Pandavas' share
Draupadi.fact: Krishna, acting as a peace emissary, attempted to negotiate with Dhritarashtra, seeking to secure the Pandavas' share.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Though an extremely powerful and symbolic theme, this incident does not appear in Vyasa's _____
Draupadi.fact: Though an extremely powerful and symbolic theme, this incident does not appear in Vyasa's Sanskrit Mahabharata.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Since then, this powerful theme of vengeance had been used in most retellings and adaptations on _____, thus mistakenly attributing the authorship to Veda Vyasa
Draupadi.fact: Though an extremely powerful and symbolic theme, this incident does not appear in Vyasa's Sanskrit Mahabharata. Since then, this powerful theme of vengeance had been used in most retellings and adaptations on Mahabharat, thus mistakenly attributing the authorship to Veda Vyasa.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Ashwathama killed _____, Shikhandi, Draupadeyas, and the remaining Pandava and Panchala army
Draupadi.fact: Ashwathama killed Dhrishtadyumna, Shikhandi, Draupadeyas, and the remaining Pandava and Panchala army.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: The Pandavas find _____ at Vyasa's hut
Draupadi.fact: Draupadi vows that if the Pandavas do not kill Ashwatthama, she would fast to death. The Pandavas find Ashwatthama at Vyasa's hut.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Arjuna and _____ end up firing the Brahmashirsha astra at each other
Draupadi.fact: Draupadi vows that if the Pandavas do not kill Ashwatthama, she would fast to death. The Pandavas find Ashwatthama at Vyasa's hut.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Not endowed with the knowledge to do so, _____ instead redirects the weapon to Uttara's womb, but Krishna protects the Pandavas' only heir with his Sudarshana Chakra
Draupadi.fact: The Pandavas find Ashwatthama at Vyasa's hut. Arjuna and Ashwatthama end up firing the Brahmashirsha astra at each other.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Ashwatthama is caught by the _____ and his jewel is taken away
Draupadi.fact: Not endowed with the knowledge to do so, Ashwatthama instead redirects the weapon to Uttara's womb, but Krishna protects the Pandavas' only heir with his Sudarshana Chakra. Ashwatthama is caught by the Pandavas and his jewel is taken away.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Due to the power of meditation, her wrath is subdued and she speaks of _____, son of their preceptor Drona, "I desired to only pay off our debt for the injury we have sustained
Draupadi.fact: Due to the power of meditation, her wrath is subdued and she speaks of Ashwathama, son of their preceptor Drona, "I desired to only pay off our debt for the injury we have sustained.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: When her husbands retired from the world and went on their journey towards the _____ and heaven, she accompanied them and was the first to fall dead on the journey
Draupadi.fact: When her husbands retired from the world and went on their journey towards the Himalayas and heaven, she accompanied them and was the first to fall dead on the journey.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: The rituals are quite unique and aren't typical of the wider _____ community
Draupadi.fact: The rituals are quite unique and aren't typical of the wider Tamil community. This tradition is widespread, with over 400 temples dedicated to Draupadi in South Indian states such as Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, and Karnataka, as well as in countries with a large Tamil population like Sri Lanka, Singapore, Malaysia, Mauritius, Réunion, and South Africa.

Draupadi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Draupadi.question: Notably, fire walking or _____ is a prominent ritual performed at these temples
Draupadi.fact: Notably, fire walking or Thimithi is a prominent ritual performed at these temples.
